### Fire-and-forget chain can now reject unhandled via unguarded Mongo reads

**Warning Severity**

`enrolInMonitoringPortfolio` is invoked detached (`void this.enrolInMonitoringPortfolio(...)`), and the new fall-through now awaits `removeSupersededCompany` after the try/catch, where `creditsafeReport.distinct` and the `findOne` calls inside `matchIsStillClaimed` run outside any error handling. A Mongo failure on those reads rejects the detached promise with no handler — every promise must have error handling, and before this change the only fallible operation in the detached chain (the vendor add) was fully guarded.

**Fix:**
```
Wrap the `removeSupersededCompany` call (or its `distinct`/`matchIsStillClaimed` reads) in a try/catch that logs, matching the guard already applied to the vendor calls in the same detached chain.
```

Agreed, fixed. A 404 here is now counted as `outcome:already_absent` and no longer logged as a failure, with `outcome:failure` kept for every other status — covered by two new cases.

Worth recording why the status is safe to read that way on this path, since the vendor declares the 404 on `DELETE /monitoring/portfolios/{portfolioId}/companies/{companyId}` without describing what raises it, and its 404 elsewhere means the portfolio itself is unknown (`packages/creditsafe-sdk/README.md:382`). A concurrent `selectCompany` onto that same `connectId` can write and enrol after the claim check and before the delete, so the new claimant is left unmonitored. comments.author: robinthiry-naboo
comments.body:
Known and accepted, and worth writing down this time — Bugbot raised the same race earlier on this PR and it was resolved without a note, which is why it came back.

The window is real: the claim check reads other venues' latest rows, and a concurrent `selectCompany` onto the same `connectId` can enrol between that read and the vendor `DELETE`. Closing it properly needs a lock across the vendor call, which this PR is not the place for.

What makes it tolerable is that the repair already exists and is add-only: `reconcile-portfolio.ts` only ever calls `addPortfolioCompany` (line 97) and never `removePortfolioCompany`, so a company dropped by this race is re-enrolled on the next reconciliation rather than left out. Running that reconciliation on a cron is RAR-1411, in progress.

The residual exposure is what you name: alerts raised in the gap resolve through `connectId`, so a venue can miss events until the reconciliation runs. That is the cost being accepted, not an oversight.

### [BUG-001] A skipped removal is never retried, and nothing reconciles the surplus: Medium

**Confidence:** HIGH

**Issue:** this comment says a company left behind is "the drift RAR-1399's reconciliation half is there to catch", but `reconcilePortfolio` stays add-only: its dependency is `Pick<CreditsafeService, 'addPortfolioCompany' | 'listPortfolioCompanies'>` and `driftCount` only counts partners missing from the portfolio. The comment added at `reconcile-portfolio.ts:127-132` says the opposite ("nothing here counts a company the portfolio holds that nothing selects any more"). Ticket piece (2), "the surplus in `reconcilePortfolio` ... a diff against the selected connect ids", is not in this PR.

The removal candidate is only ever the latest row at selection time, so once that row moves on, the old company is never looked at again. Traced path:
1. Venue bound to A (enrolled). Admin re-selects B, `addPortfolioCompany` answers 503: early `return` at L378, A kept (intended, pinned by the test at L852). Row B is already written (L191, awaited before the detached call).
2. Admin refreshes B later: `supersededConnectId === connectId` (both B), early `return` at L416.
3. A stays in the portfolio for good.

Same end state for a non-404 DELETE failure (logged here, never retried). The reconcile comment also understates the residue: it is not only "a removal the vendor refused", it includes every failed add followed by a refresh.

**Impact:** a billed monitored line nobody watches, and rating events on A resolved through `connectId` to a venue that is no longer A once RAR-1197's poll ships, which is exactly what this PR sets out to prevent. No metric counts the surplus, so it is silent.

**Fix:** either implement piece (2) (surplus = enrolled ids minus latest selected ids, counted in the drift or its own metric, removed only under `isConfirmed`, `Pick` widened to `removePortfolioCompany`), or get the de-scope explicitly agreed on the ticket with a follow-up, and correct this comment so it does not promise a catch that does not exist.

comments.body:
### The superseded read can fail the selection after the CreditSafe credit is spent

**Medium Severity**

This `findOne` exists only to feed the detached monitoring chain, but it is awaited on the mutation's critical path — after `getReport` (`:160`) has already spent a billed CreditSafe credit — and it carries no `.catch()`. Any rejection (query timeout, read-preference hiccup) propagates straight out of `selectCompany`.

The file treats both properties as contracts in its own comments: *"an unknown `houseId` costs no CreditSafe credit"* and *"on failure nothing is written"*. The second still holds; the first no longer does. Before this PR nothing between `getReport` and `create` could reject this way, so a Mongo blip on a read that serves only best-effort monitoring now fails the whole admin selection: no report row, no audit entry, no billing autofill, and the credit burnt.

The new detached-chain test covers a rejecting `distinct`, but not a rejecting `findOne` — that one no longer reaches the chain.

**Fix:** move the read above the `getReport` call at `:160`. Nothing writes to `creditsafeReport` between the two points, so the read-before-the-write property it needs is preserved, and a read failure then costs nothing.

A `.catch(() => null)` at the read site also works, but silently degrades monitoring instead of failing loudly, so the move is the better of the two.

comments.author: robinthiry-naboo
comments.body:
Agreed, and the property you quote is the right frame: the file promises "an unknown `houseId` costs no CreditSafe credit", and this read broke it by sitting between the billed call and the write.

Moved above `getReport` rather than wrapped, for the reason you give — a `.catch(() => null)` keeps the selection alive but degrades monitoring silently, and a superseded company that is silently forgotten is exactly the bug this PR exists to fix. Nothing writes to `creditsafeReport` between the old and new positions, so the read-before-the-write property it needs is untouched.

You are also right that the detached-chain test does not cover this: it rejects `distinct`, which runs inside the chain. After the move a rejecting `findOne` fails the mutation before any credit is spent, which the existing "should write nothing when the vendor call fails" shape already covers from the other side.

comments.body:
Agreed, and the fix is the read moved back down — under `getReport`, next to the write it feeds.

The scenario holds exactly as you describe it. Venue on company A, two selections overlapping the vendor round trip: the first reads `A`, the second also reads `A` (nothing has written yet), writes its row and removes `A`; the first then writes its own row and removes `A` again — a 404, counted `already_absent`. One premise of the counter-argument that put the read up there needs correcting, though — it is what makes the move safe. The read was raised above `getReport` so a Mongo failure could not sink a mutation whose CreditSafe credit was already spent. But that property was already gone: `house.findById` is awaited between the billed call and the write, with no `.catch()`, and has been since before this PR.

https://github.com/naboo-team/naboo/blob/da16683b553e090d2c2c20a438b792e823ee367e/packages/wome-api/src/domain-modules/listing/house/sub-modules/house-partner-health/sub-modules/creditsafe-report/services/creditsafe-report.service.ts#L172-L191

If Mongo is down at that point the `create` two statements later fails anyway, so the credit is lost either way. Putting the superseded read beside it therefore costs nothing that still stands, and the promise the file actually makes — an unknown `houseId` costs no CreditSafe credit — is carried by the opening `findById`, which has not moved.

What remains is the read-then-create window, which is the same family as the claim-check race already accepted on this PR: closing it needs a lock spanning the vendor call, out of scope here.

comments.body:
RAR-1399 Remove a company from the monitoring portfolio when a venue is re-selected

Enrolment is add-only today, so a venue re-selected onto a different company stays monitored on the first one — billed, and attributable. ## What happens An admin picks company A for venue X by mistake, then re-selects the right company B. `selectCompany` appends a second report row and posts B into the portfolio. Nothing removes A. The venue is now bound to B — its most recent row — while the portfolio holds both. Two costs follow: * **A is still monitored**, so the recurring vendor spend continues for a company nobody watches. * ⚠️ **Once [RAR-1197]()'s poll attributes notifications through the** `connectId` **index, a rating move on A raises an alert against X.** X's superseded row still carries A and is not deleted, so the lookup resolves. The alert names a venue on the strength of a click that was corrected. ## Why the drift check cannot see it `reconcilePortfolio` counts partners *selected but missing from the portfolio*. This is the opposite direction — *held by the portfolio but no longer selected*. The backlog script reads one row per venue sorted on `fetchedAt`, so it only ever sees B, classifies the venue `alreadyEnrolled`, and reports `drift: 0`. The blind spot is structural, not a bug in the counter. ## What it takes CreditSafe exposes the removal, our SDK simply does not wrap it yet: `DELETE /monitoring/portfolios/{portfolioId}/companies/{companyId}` — *Delete Company From Portfolio*, declared in both Connect 1.10.9 and Global Monitoring 1.0.0. The `{companyId}` path parameter takes *"A company Safe Number or Connect ID"*, so the stored `connectId` works as-is. Declared responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404 — a 404 for a company already absent makes a re-run safe. Three pieces: 1. `removePortfolioCompany` on the SDK monitoring resource and on `CreditsafeService`. 2. The surplus in `reconcilePortfolio`: the membership set is already read, so it is a diff against the selected connect ids. 3. The removal itself, plus whether it belongs on the live selection path or only in the reconciliation run — a live removal on every re-selection spends a vendor call on an event nobody measured yet. ⚠️ **Not urgent while the poll is unshipped.** The estate is 75 venues and the second cost above is the one that bites; the first is small. This was found during review of [RAR-1192]() and deliberately left out of it to keep that PR scoped.

Review in Linear
